short: The longest dynasty in Chinese history, and the source of the Mandate of Heaven.
full:
The Zhou overthrew the Shang at the battle of Muye in about 1046 BCE and justified the conquest with an idea that outlived them by three thousand years: Heaven grants the right to rule to whoever governs well, and withdraws it from whoever does not. The Mandate of Heaven made every later rebellion arguable and every later dynasty answerable. The Zhou kings granted territories to kinsmen and allies who owed military service in return, a settlement that worked while the royal house was strong.

In 771 BCE Quanrong raiders sacked the western capital near modern Xi'an and killed King You. The court moved east to Luoyi, and the Eastern Zhou that followed was a kingship in name only: the vassal states fought, absorbed one another and eventually claimed the royal title themselves. The dynasty's last four centuries are conventionally divided into the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods. Qin armies took the Zhou domain in 256 BCE and King Nan died the same year, ending a nominal reign of nearly eight hundred years.
